briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 2, 2026. Today's briefing will cover a wide range of topics, from the severe impacts of climate change both domestically and internationally, to various efforts towards carbon neutrality, and significant progress in renewable energy transition.

sections.title: 🔴 Urgent Climate Crisis Warnings and Impacts
sections.content: Domestically and internationally, threats to food security and ecosystem disruptions due to climate change are intensifying. The aftermath of 'Super El Niño' is raising concerns about sugar and rice shortages, which are expected to continue into next year [1], and domestic ecosystems are facing severe threats, with a sharp increase in forest damage caused by invasive pests such as the spotted lanternfly and the fall webworm [15, 18]. In particular, the seas around Jeju are already transforming into subtropical waters, directly impacted by global warming [17]. The climate crisis is shattering the 'resilience illusion' of South Korea's supply chains and affecting corporate strategies [7]. Internationally, the costs of climate change are already immense, with Europe experiencing its worst heatwave on record, leading to fatalities and crop failures [140], and critical supply chains are threatened by climate change and geopolitical instability [134].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Efforts for Climate Change Adaptation and Response
sections.content: Various local governments and institutions in South Korea are continuing their efforts to strengthen climate change adaptation and response capabilities. Gongju City hosted special lectures for citizens to enhance their climate crisis response capabilities [2, 23, 24], and Ulsan City significantly raised its disaster prevention performance targets to respond to climate change [5]. Technological responses are also active, with products like 'Ami65' stably managing crop growth even in abnormal weather conditions [4]. K-water has introduced AI-based digital water management to respond to climate crisis phenomena such as floods and droughts [16]. Research on ecosystem changes is also underway; a long-term survey will begin in Gwangryeocheon to identify changes in freshwater snail habitats due to climate change [3]. International cooperation is also being strengthened, with K-water expanding AI and digital water management collaboration with five Mekong countries [22].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating the Transition to a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: Various local governments and companies in South Korea are actively moving towards achieving carbon neutrality goals. Busan New Port is planned to be developed as a carbon-neutral industrial hub [25, 26, 35, 36, 47, 61]. Nowon-gu participated in the EU Green Day Festival, showcasing its achievements as a leading carbon-neutral city and its goal to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 40% by 2030 [19, 31, 38, 45, 53, 57, 73, 74]. Seongnam City is seeking solutions by hosting a citizen-participation carbon neutrality idea contest [28, 29, 30, 50, 55, 64, 66, 67]. Ganghwa County is pursuing 'Ganghwa-type carbon neutrality' linking agriculture, forestry, and tidal flats, with a goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 36.4% by 2034 [52]. However, regional disparities exist, with Chungbuk province's carbon neutrality achievement rate at 60.5%, ranking among the lowest nationwide [41]. Concerns have also been raised that the controversy over Canada's taxonomy could affect South Korea's carbon-neutral financial policies [39].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Power Grid Innovation
sections.content: Large-scale projects and policy changes are continuing to accelerate the domestic renewable energy transition. One year after its establishment, the Ministry of Climate is accelerating the 100GW renewable energy transition, overhauling solar regulations and grid systems [82]. In preparation for the 100GW renewable energy era, a 'major overhaul' is underway, including a complete reorganization of the power grid connection system [85]. In particular, Goheung County is actively pursuing a 10GW renewable energy plan and promoting a 'citizen energy pension' [78, 84, 89, 92, 93, 94, 97, 100, 101, 104, 106, 108, 115, 116], thereby building an innovative win-win model. In Jeju, the connection with hydrogen energy is being strengthened, with water electrolysis being utilized as a power grid flexibility resource to respond to renewable energy variability, and full-scale development of clean hydrogen production technology commencing [77, 79, 86, 99]. Meanwhile, challenges remain, such as the controversy over funding for regional tariff systems due to industrial electricity rate discounts [111] and criticism regarding the Korea Rural Community Corporation's obligation to supply renewable energy [87].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Climate Response and Discourse
sections.content: The international community is responding to the complex impacts of climate change, and South Korea is also strengthening international cooperation, including hosting a high-level forum on green transition and climate action with the European Union [135]. In the scientific community, metal-organic interactions have been identified as a key factor in the carbon cycle, contributing to improved climate change predictions [125]. Research has also been published showing that self-organized landscape patterns help plants adapt to climate change [138]. Meanwhile, warnings about the implications of global warming exceeding 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels [130] and that historical fossil fuel emissions could impact global warming until 2500 [126] underscore the urgency of climate action. Cultural discourse is also forming, with the release of the film 'Digger' on the theme of climate change [124, 129, 136]. Grassroots adaptation efforts are also continuing, with the City of Cincinnati providing financial support to residents for climate change response [122] and Berlin citizens using an app to care for street trees [141].

briefing.closing: As we have seen in today's briefing, climate change is having severe impacts across our society, but at the same time, diverse domestic and international efforts to address it are ongoing. Continued interest and participation in climate action will be crucial moving forward. This concludes today's climate briefing.
